learn.title: Solar PV and the Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity, making them the fastest-growing power source worldwide. Understanding the photoelectric effect reveals how silicon atoms release electrons when struck by photons, turning sunshine into usable current for homes, factories and entire cities.
learn.c1_text: When sunlight hits a solar cell, photons carry energy into silicon atoms. If a photon has enough energy, it knocks an electron free from its atom. This is the photoelectric effect, first explained by Einstein in 1905, the same physics now powering rooftops from Delhi to Denver.
learn.c2_text: A solar cell has two silicon layers, one with extra electrons (n-type) and one missing electrons (p-type). This built-in electric field pushes freed electrons in one direction, creating direct current. Multiple cells wired together form a panel that typically produces 400 to 600 watts under full sun.
learn.c3_title: 🇮🇳 India Scales Solar at Record Speed
learn.c3_text: India operates one of the world's largest solar parks, Bhadla in Rajasthan, spanning 14,000 acres with 2.25 GW capacity. The PM Surya Ghar scheme targets 10 million rooftop installations, letting households earn income by selling excess solar power back to the grid under net metering rules.

learn.stat2: A typical solar panel is about 20-22% efficient at converting sunlight

learn.stat4: Global solar PV capacity passed 1.6 TW in 2024, the largest renewable source

learn.title: Capacity Factor: Rated Power vs Real Output
learn.intro: A 100 MW solar farm rarely produces 100 MW. Capacity factor measures how much electricity a plant actually generates compared to its nameplate rating, and understanding it is critical for comparing solar, wind, and coal fairly when planning the clean energy transition.
learn.c1_text: If a 100 MW solar farm generates 250 GWh in a year, the capacity factor is about 28%. Think of it like a car's fuel efficiency: the engine size is rated power, but real driving conditions determine actual mileage. Weather, night, and seasons all reduce real output below nameplate capacity.
learn.c2_text: Utility solar typically has a 20-30% capacity factor because it only produces during daylight. Onshore wind averages 25-40%, offshore wind reaches 40-55%, and nuclear runs at 85-93% almost continuously. A low capacity factor does not mean poor economics, since solar's fuel is free and abundant.
learn.c3_text: Indian solar plants achieve 18-25% capacity factors, lower than sunny deserts but competitive in monsoon-affected regions. Rajasthan and Gujarat exceed 25%, while Kerala and Tamil Nadu fall below 20% due to cloud cover. Planners add battery storage to firm up supply during evening peak demand.
learn.stat1: US utility-scale solar averaged 23.5% capacity factor in 2023
learn.stat2: Nuclear plants typically achieve 85-93% capacity factor globally
learn.stat3: Offshore wind farms can reach 55% capacity factor in good sites
learn.stat4: India's solar capacity factors range from 18% in cloudy regions to 25% in Rajasthan

learn.title: Solid-State Batteries: Safer, Denser Power
learn.intro: Solid-state batteries replace liquid electrolytes with solid materials, promising higher energy density, faster charging, and dramatically lower fire risk. They could double EV range and transform grid storage, making renewable energy more practical across transport, homes, and heavy industry.
learn.c1_text: Conventional lithium-ion batteries use a flammable liquid electrolyte that can ignite when damaged. Solid-state batteries swap this for ceramic, sulfide, or polymer materials. The result is a non-flammable cell that resists thermal runaway, the chain reaction that causes EV battery fires.
learn.c2_text: Solid electrolytes enable lithium-metal anodes, which store roughly 10 times more energy than graphite. This could push EV range past 1,000 km per charge. Solid-state cells also tolerate more charge cycles, with lab prototypes exceeding 10,000 cycles compared to 1,000-2,000 for current lithium-ion cells.
learn.c3_text: India's PLI scheme allocates 18,100 crore rupees to advanced chemistry cell manufacturing, including solid-state research. The India Energy Storage Alliance targets 60 GWh of domestic battery capacity by 2030. Bengaluru-based firms are piloting solid-state prototypes for two-wheeler EVs and grid applications.
learn.stat1: Solid-state prototypes have reached 500 Wh/kg energy density vs 250 Wh/kg for lithium-ion
learn.stat2: Global investment in solid-state batteries exceeded 7 billion USD in 2023
learn.stat3: India targets 60 GWh of battery manufacturing capacity by 2030

learn.title: Hydrogen Fuel Cells: Clean Power Onboard
learn.intro: Hydrogen fuel cells combine hydrogen and oxygen to generate electricity, emitting only water vapor. They offer zero-emission power for trucks, buses, and trains where batteries are too heavy, providing a vital pathway to decarbonize long-distance transport and heavy industry globally.
learn.c1_text: A fuel cell works like a battery that never runs flat as long as hydrogen is supplied. Hydrogen enters the anode, oxygen at the cathode, and a catalyst splits the hydrogen into protons and electrons. Electrons flow through a motor, producing power, while protons combine with oxygen to form pure water.
learn.c2_text: A hydrogen fuel cell vehicle carries a 5-10 kg tank, refuels in 5-10 minutes, and travels 500-700 km. Battery electric trucks would need several tonnes of batteries for similar range, making fuel cells attractive for long-haul trucking, mining dump trucks, intercity buses, and regional passenger trains.
learn.c3_text: India launched the National Green Hydrogen Mission in 2023 with 19,744 crore rupees to produce 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen by 2030. Reliance, Adani, and NTPC are building pilot projects in Gujarat, while Indian Railways is testing hydrogen fuel cell trains on the Jind-Sonipat route in Haryana.
learn.stat1: A hydrogen fuel cell bus is 30-40% more efficient than a diesel engine
learn.stat2: India targets 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen production by 2030
learn.stat3: Toyota Mirai fuel cell car has a range of 650 km per refill
learn.stat4: Global hydrogen demand reached 95 million tonnes in 2023, mostly for fertilizers

learn.title: Virtual Power Plants: Smart Distributed Energy
learn.intro: Virtual Power Plants use artificial intelligence to coordinate millions of rooftop solar panels, batteries, EVs, and smart appliances, turning small distributed devices into one large flexible power source. They are reshaping how grids balance supply and demand in the renewable energy era.
learn.c1_text: Imagine coordinating 1 million home solar systems, 500,000 home batteries, and 200,000 EVs as if they were a single 5 GW power station. AI software forecasts solar output, predicts demand, and dispatches stored energy within milliseconds, responding to grid signals and earning revenue for participating households.
learn.c2_text: Vehicle-to-grid or V2G technology lets EVs sell stored electricity back during peak hours. Smart water heaters, AC units, and pool pumps automatically pause when prices spike. This demand response can shave 10-15% off peak demand without anyone noticing, while reducing the need for new fossil fuel peaker plants.
learn.c3_text: India's first commercial VPP is being deployed in Delhi and Mumbai using aggregated rooftop solar and battery systems. Tata Power and BSES are piloting programs where 10,000-plus households collectively bid into power exchanges. The CEA estimates VPPs could provide 30 GW of flexibility by 2030 across Indian states.
learn.stat1: Global VPP capacity is forecast to reach 30-80 GW by 2030
learn.stat2: Australia's AGL VPP coordinates over 10,000 home batteries delivering 1 GW
learn.stat3: India targets 30 GW of virtual power plant capacity by 2030
learn.stat4: V2G could return 12 billion USD annually to US EV owners by 2030

learn.title: LCOE: Comparing Energy Sources Fairly
learn.intro: How do you fairly compare a solar plant, a coal plant, and a wind farm? The Levelised Cost of Energy crunches all lifetime costs and total electricity generated into a single per-unit price, revealing that renewables are now the cheapest option in most countries worldwide.
learn.c1_title: 💰 All Costs Over a Plant's Life
learn.c1_text: LCOE divides total lifetime costs, including capital, fuel, operations, maintenance, and decommissioning, by total electricity generated over the plant's life. It is like a loan EMI calculator for power plants. A lower LCOE means cheaper electricity, helping policymakers and investors choose between technologies fairly.
learn.c2_text: Utility-scale solar LCOE fell from 0.45 USD/kWh in 2010 to 0.04-0.05 USD/kWh by 2023, an 89% drop. Onshore wind dropped similarly. New coal plants typically cost 0.06-0.12 USD/kWh. IRENA data shows 81% of new renewable projects in 2023 produced cheaper electricity than any new fossil fuel alternative.
learn.c3_text: India has seen some of the world's lowest solar tariffs, with Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Park auctioning at 2.97 INR/kWh in 2017. Bhadla Phase III hit a record 2.44 INR/kWh. SECI auctions in 2024 saw solar tariffs around 2.50 INR/kWh, undercutting new coal plants in most Indian states significantly.
learn.stat1: Global utility solar LCOE averaged 0.044 USD/kWh in 2023
learn.stat2: Onshore wind LCOE fell to 0.033 USD/kWh globally in 2023
learn.stat3: India's Bhadla solar auction hit 2.44 INR/kWh, among world's lowest
